text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: inference-routing-usw - error-rate > 5% (auto-threshold). Pager key: PDX3k. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PDX3k
Maria: Acking this oncall, taking it now. I'll check routing pools + autoscaler.
Dan: seeing a quick spike in KV-miss warms around the same time in grafana: https://grafana.example/d/abc123/inference - looks like a warmup wave from canary traffic.
Maria: Confirmed ~3m latency/error bump starting 20:41 UTC. Autoscaler fired one scale-up at 20:43 and error rate dropped shortly after.
Kevin: quick query shows ~112 5xxs in that 3m window for us-west. Not huge but noticeable.
Maria: Checking customer logs for correlated 5xxs — nothing obvious tied to a single customer id so far. No SLO breach alerts triggered.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident auto-resolved (alert no longer firing).
Maria: Good, looks auto-resolved once the scaler stabilized. I'll keep a 30m watchwindow. No immediate customer-impact flags. :thumbsup:
Sara: This is noisy recurring pattern — KV warmup + autoscaler race. Can we add a short suppression or increase the cooldown on the metric? cc @oncall-team
Maria: Agree. Filing follow-up INF-2945: "Transient route error bursts from KV warmup -> suggest metric cooldown + debounce". I'll attach graphs and the timeline.
Dan: If we want to be able to mute these faster, quick PD silence via API:
```
curl -X POST "https://api.pagerduty.com/maintenance_windows" 
 -H "Accept: application/vnd.pagerduty+json;version=2" 
 -H "Authorization: Token token=REDACTED" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"maintenance_window": {"type":"maintenance_window","start_time":"2025-01-01T20:45:00Z","end_time":"2025-01-01T21:15:00Z","services":[{"id":"PABC","type":"service_reference"}]}}'
```
Dan: we should keep that as a last resort if noise ramps up.
Maria: Handing off monitoring to Kevin — I'm stepping away in ~20m for dinner. Will check remote if it fires again. :wave:
Kevin: Acknowledged, I'll watch the dashboards for 2 hours and escalate if it flares back up.
Sara: Thanks — also adding a small runbook note to INF-2945 recommending a short-term suppression and a longer-term fix (increase KV cache warmup, tweak autoscaler window). :memo:
